anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither fact moved. In both outputs the post-merge cleanup row reads exactly 'tear down the gate's checkout and local branch (untracked files there are deleted)' with [recommended], and the cleanup execution runs only the worktree, branch, and base steps, explicitly noting the absence of a `## cleanup` section so no override step is attempted. After preserves the row wording and the steps-1-3-only statement verbatim in substance. One non-graded difference worth noting: After drops the pre-removal guards Before showed (the tracked-clean `status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` check and the `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <assessed-sha>` check before `worktree remove --force`), and also drops the post-prune `worktree list --porcelain` confirmation; if the Change intends terminal cleanup ownership to stay unchanged, keep those guard commands in the cleanup block so the destructive remove is visibly gated on the same evidence as before, while still rendering the shared menus.md templates.

To keep f2 unambiguous while still delivering the shared-menu migration, have the cleanup record end with a one-line overrides status (e.g. "overrides: none (no ## cleanup section at merge-base)") alongside the worktree/branch/base lines, so the ordered-overrides ownership is visibly exercised and reported as empty rather than omitted.
